memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Then the Lord said to Moses, 'Make a bronze basin, with its bronze stand, for washing. Place it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water in it. Aaron and his sons are to wash their hands and feet with water from it.'" - Exodus 30:17-19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
A bronze basin stood between the altar and the tent, filled with water for washing. The priests had already been washed once at their ordination, thoroughly and completely. Yet daily, before every act of service, they washed again. One cleansing had made them priests; ongoing washing kept them fit to serve.

Jesus drew on this distinction beautifully. When Peter objected to having his feet washed, Jesus replied that those who have had a bath need only wash their feet; their whole body is clean (John 13:10). One decisive cleansing, then ongoing washing for the dust picked up along the way.

This is a great comfort. If you belong to Christ, you do not need to be saved again every time you sin. That washing was complete and permanent. But you do need the daily washing of confession, because we pick up dust simply by walking through this world. John writes that if we confess our sins, God is faithful and just and will forgive us and purify us (1 John 1:9). Come to the basin daily. The bath was once; the washing is ongoing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Am I confusing my need for daily cleansing with a need to be saved again?
Is confession a regular part of my walk with God, or something I avoid?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my cleansing in Christ is complete and permanent. Teach me to come daily for the washing of confession, keeping short accounts with You. Amen.
